title: Libra Community Mandate v0.1
description: A machine-readable rulebook in which a public body or community, not the audited company or its auditor, fixes every parameter that decides whether a published AI bias audit passes. Evidence (the company's published counts) and rules (the mandate) are kept separate, so any audit can be judged under any mandate.

status.description: descriptive = encodes what current law permits; illustrative = example, adopted by no one; draft = under deliberation; adopted = ratified by the authority named below, with a public record.

process.description: How the rules were decided: hearing, assembly vote, consent process, rulemaking.

record_uri.description: Public record of the decision (minutes, vote, rulemaking docket). Required for status=adopted.

reading.description: point = compare the bare published ratio; interval = require the uncertainty interval to settle the question.

alpha.description: Two-sided error level for intervals (0.10 = 90% intervals). Ignored for point reading.

familywise.description: Adjust for the number of comparisons in an audit (Bonferroni).

comparator_rule.description: Which group is the reference: highest rate among eligible groups, or among all groups.

small_category_exclusion.description: Share of applicants below which a group is dropped from the calculations; null = never drop. Under NYC LL144 this is at the auditor's discretion (6 RCNY 5-301(d)).

indeterminate_is.description: Who carries the burden when the evidence cannot settle the question.

accept_test_data.description: Whether an audit built on test or unknown data, rather than real applicant data, can satisfy the mandate.

rationale.description: Why each rule was chosen, in the authority's own words. Keys mirror rules.
